question: Should OpenClaw V1 make `api.registerReadinessCriterion` plus `gateway.readiness` selector identifiers a supported public plugin and operator contract, or should plugin-provided criteria be deferred from the initial readiness feature?
rationale: This is a durable SDK and configuration commitment with upgrade and provider-behavior consequences; source review can assess mechanics but cannot choose the permanent product boundary.

options.title: Approve the public readiness contract
options.body: Accept the Plugin SDK callback and selector identifiers as supported V1 surface, then require current-head compatibility and recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Land core-only readiness first
options.body: Defer plugin registration and its Policy example until maintainers separately approve a plugin-facing readiness contract.

options.title: Pause the readiness stack
options.body: Defer both the owner-adoption and profile follow-ons until the RFC direction has explicit maintainer sponsorship.

recommendation.title: Approve the public readiness contract
recommendation.body: Accept the Plugin SDK callback and selector identifiers as supported V1 surface, then require current-head compatibility and recovery proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked framework and this adoption layer, so they are the clearest contributor to route the decision to the appropriate OpenClaw core and Plugin SDK owner.
